title: Science Investigation Quiz
subtitle: 50 multiple-choice questions from Chapter 1
introText: Review science, the scientific method, experiments, graphs, laboratory tools, and safety. Choose the best answer to each question.

questions.question: What does it mean to investigate something?
options: Change facts to match an idea
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 2.

questions.question: Which example shows technology?
options: Noticing that a leaf is green
Asking why the sky is blue
Using a wheel to move a cart
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 2.

questions.question: Which list names the three main branches of natural science?
options: Earth science, life science, and physical science
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 5.

questions.question: Which branch of science studies living things?
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 5.

questions.question: Which branch studies Earth, its atmosphere, and outer space?

questions.question: What does physical science study?

Only the parts of the human body

questions.question: What did Copernicus conclude about Earth and the other planets?
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 3.

questions.question: Which activity belongs to the first step of the scientific method?
options: Decide that a hypothesis is correct
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 3.

questions.question: What is a hypothesis?
options: A reasonable prediction that can be tested
A final decision based on results
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 4.

questions.question: Why should a scientist research before forming a hypothesis?
options: To base the prediction on useful information
To guarantee the prediction is correct
To avoid ever doing an experiment
To replace all observations with guesses
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 8.

questions.question: In the hypothesis "If I give a plant more sunlight, then it will grow taller," what is the predicted effect?
options: The plant is placed in a pot
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 4.

questions.question: What should a scientist do after forming a hypothesis?
options: Declare the prediction a scientific law
Plan an experiment and collect data
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 4.

questions.question: Which example is data collected during an experiment?
options: A record of plant heights measured each week
A question about what might happen
A guess made before any observation
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 4.

questions.question: Which question is open-ended?
options: Is the pot made of clay?
Did you water the plant today?
How does the amount of water affect plant growth?
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 8.

questions.question: What is the independent variable in a fair experiment?

questions.question: What is a dependent variable?

questions.question: What is another name for controlled variables?

questions.question: Why should only one factor be changed at a time in a fair experiment?
options: To help identify what caused the results
To make the control group unnecessary

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a control group?
options: To provide a standard for comparison

questions.question: Which group tests the changed factor?
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 9.

questions.question: A student gives similar plants different amounts of water. What is the independent variable?

The size of the identical pots

questions.question: A student measures how tall each plant grows after changing the amount of water. What is the dependent variable?
options: Type of soil kept the same

questions.question: When testing how water amounts affect plant growth, which factors should stay the same?
options: Water amount, plant height, and results

questions.question: Why do scientists repeat an experiment?
options: To check whether the results are consistent
To change every variable at once
To make an incorrect result become correct

questions.question: A toy car takes 6, 7, and 8 seconds to finish three runs. What is its average time?

questions.question: Why do scientists use standard units of measurement?
options: So every experiment has the same result
So people can understand and compare shared data
So they can avoid writing down numbers

A list of laboratory safety rules only

options: A decrease followed by a decrease

questions.question: What should a scientific conclusion be based on?
options: The first idea that came to mind
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 16.

questions.question: What does inconclusive mean?
options: The experiment needs no more work
Every measurement is exactly the same
There is not enough clear evidence to reach a conclusion
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 16.

questions.question: Repeated results do not support a hypothesis. What should the scientist do?
options: Keep only the results that fit the prediction
Review the evidence and form a new hypothesis to test

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares scientific laws and theories?
options: Laws are guesses; theories are lists of equipment
Laws are laboratory rules; theories are measuring tools
Laws and theories both describe only living things
Laws describe patterns in nature; theories explain why they occur
questions.sourceNote: Based on the supplied Science Investigation chapter, printed page 17.

questions.question: Why do scientists share their results?
options: So they can replace evidence with opinions
So nobody needs to repeat experiments
So others can compare data and test their ideas

questions.question: Which student is following laboratory safety rules?
options: A student running while carrying a flask
A student tasting an unknown liquid
A student pouring leftover chemicals down the drain
A student wearing goggles and closed-toe shoes with long hair tied back
